## ⚠ The `prose-only` register

**31 of 32 standards contain rules nothing checks.** That is the gap between what this
repository says it enforces and what it does.

**The ratchet:** a `prose-only` rule that survives two consecutive checkpoint reviews without being
mechanised gets **deleted** — not weakened, deleted. An unenforced rule everyone has agreed to keep is
worse than no rule, because it creates the impression of a standard where none exists.

Every standard declares a `disposition` saying what becomes of its unenforced rules:

| Verdict | Standards | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mechanise` | 15 | Becomes a check. The mechanism is named in the disposition. |
| `reference` | 4 | Stays as consult-on-demand reference; not rules an agent must follow while working. |
| `delete` | 0 | To be removed. An unenforced rule creates the impression of a standard where none exists. |
| `keep` | 13 | Judgement that cannot be mechanised, with the reason it is load-bearing anyway. |

| Standard | Lines | Other enforcement | Disposition |
